predecessors.name: Ottoman Empire
predecessors.text: the Sanjak of Bosnia (1463) with the Duchy of Herzegovina (1483) and the Slavonian, Lika and Dalmatian sanjaks around it

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina, which 'nominally remain[ed] under sovereignty of the Ottoman Empire' after the Treaty of Berlin (1878)

ledger.x: 1580: the Sanjak of Bosnia becomes an eyalet under Ferhad Pasha Sokolović.
1669: the Candia War peace; the page names no place gained, so the region is the part of the Bosnia shape inside the wider Venetian circles.
30 September 1686.
September 1687.
11 September 1688.
26 November 1690.
1694: "Venice took territory north of the Republic of Ragusa".
1699 (Karlowitz): "the eyalet lost Slavonian sanjaks, the Lika sanjak, and much of the Dalmatian coast"; reduced to four sanjaks and twelve captaincies.

26 January 1699 (Karlowitz): "Venice did relinquish the areas of Popovo polje as well as Klek and Sutorina"; the land in Bosnia and Herzegovina that the 1694 Venetian shape held (the Čitluk-Gabela strip excepted) returns to the eyalet.
1703: "The seat moved from Sarajevo to Travnik after a fire"; the infobox and the body text give 1699 and 1697.
1718: the Peace of Passarowitz gives northern Bosnia to Austria; the Bosnia Eyalet page records 28 more military captaincies formed before 1718 but not the treaty.
1718: "Čitluk and Gabela were lost to the Ottomans" by the treaty (Passarowitz).
1739: northern Bosnia leaves the Habsburg frontier ("From 1718 to 1739"); the Bosnia Eyalet page is silent on the Treaty of Belgrade.
January-February 1831: the Bosnian aristocrats meet in Tuzla (20 January to 5 February) and Husein Gradaščević occupies Travnik, the seat.

1832: the page is silent on how the revolt ended; the year is bridged from the infobox (Travnik capital to 1832) and from the 1833 settlement that rewarded Rizvanbegović for helping "crush the 1831 revolt led by Husein Gradaščević".
1833: the southern part of Bosnia is given to Ali-paša Rizvanbegović as a reward for helping crush the revolt.
1850: the seat returns from Travnik to Sarajevo.
1851: the Herzegovina Eyalet is disestablished ("1833 to 1851") and reintegrated into Bosnia; the page gives no year for the reintegration itself.
1867: the eyalet becomes the Bosnia Vilayet ("formed in 1867" after the Tanzimat reforms); the page also mentions a reform of 1865.

1878: the eyalet (Bosnia Vilayet) ends as a province when Austria-Hungary occupies it: "Austria-Hungary invaded and occupied Bosnia"; formal Ottoman sovereignty lasted until the annexation of 1908 (Condominium page: the Treaty of Berlin left Bosnia and Herzegovina "nominally" under Ottoman…

wars.name: Great Turkish War
wars.outcome: The Ottoman defeat ended at Karlowitz in 1699; the eyalet lost the Slavonian sanjaks, the Lika sanjak and much of the Dalmatian coast.

wars.name: Bosnian uprising of Husein Gradaščević
wars.outcome: The rebels occupied Travnik in 1831, demanding autonomy; crushed with the help of Ali-paša Rizvanbegović, who received the Herzegovina Eyalet in 1833.

certainty.note: Sanjak frontiers against the Habsburgs and Venice moved with the campaigns of the Long Turkish and Great Turkish wars.

The Habsburg and Venetian frontier is a treaty line (Karlowitz 1699, Passarowitz 1718, Belgrade 1739); the Montenegrin and Serbian frontiers are soft, and the 1833 Herzegovina boundary is only a list of kazas.
